input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: The second Section 12.4 bars Customer from acquiring (i.e., buying from any third party) or developing any product or service competing with Vendor, for the full three-year term plus twenty-four months, across all territories, with no product-category limit and no performance-based exit. That is exclusive dealing for the whole term without a service-level or delivery exit — walk-away territory under this rule, and well beyond the fallback (defined category, 12 months, automatic termination on Vendor performance failure). It also directly contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment, so deletion restores internal consistency. Section 7.2's disclose-and-match obligation before engaging another provider operates as a right of first refusal; it is addressed under the MFN rule and is not double-counted here, and Section 2.1's take-or-pay minimum is a volume-commitment issue rather than exclusivity. Redline deletes the covenant and confirms Vendor's non-exclusive status (preferred position, per precedent seed-exclusive).

ops.oldText: During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
ops.newText: Vendor is a non-exclusive provider of the Services. Customer is free to develop, market, sell, acquire, and use any product or service, including one that competes with Vendor, and to procure services from any other supplier at any time.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a covenant barring us from acquiring or developing competing products or services for the term plus twenty-four months, which would make Cobalt our de facto exclusive supplier; our playbook position is no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on the customer, consistent with Section 12.3. We have deleted it and confirmed Vendor's non-exclusive status.
proposal.summary: Delete the Customer exclusive-dealing/non-compete covenant in the second Section 12.4 and confirm Vendor is a non-exclusive provider.
